sources.name: Vul4Py
sources.license: No repository license file or SPDX license was stated in the GitHub metadata reviewed; seek permission/terms before redistributing benchmark contents.
frameworks: Python packages and applications; includes web, protocol, serialization, crypto, CLI, and ML-adjacent projects
sources.notes: The public README describes 100 Python entries, comprising 92 CVE and 8 GHSA IDs. dataset/vul4py.csv provides vuln_id, repo_url, and fix_commit for 100 rows; upstream states each ships vulnerable/fixed revisions plus baseline and exploit tests. The 100 concrete IDs below were transcribed from that inventory, but are only Corsair candidates.

sources.name: CVEfixes v1.0.8
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 for dataset; collection code is MIT. Upstream project source licenses remain separate.
frameworks: Multi-language open-source repositories; filter relational data to Python changed files/methods and public git histories
sources.notes: Published total is 11,873 CVEs, 12,107 fixing commits, 4,249 projects, and 272 CWEs through 2024-07-23. The reported total is not a Python-only count; obtain the 12.7-GB SQL release and apply a Python/source-file and reproducibility filter.

sources.name: MoreFixes v1
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 dataset record; the Zenodo record also identifies Apache-2.0 and MIT components. Mined repositories have their own licenses.
frameworks: Multi-language GitHub repositories; filter patches/metadata to Python projects and executable revisions
sources.notes: Published total is 26,617 CVEs from 6,945 GitHub projects and 31,883 fixing commits through 2024-01-24. It offers a PostgreSQL dump and separate patch archive. This is not a Python-only count and does not itself establish that a local harness reproduces any case.

sources.name: PyPA Advisory Database
sources.available_cases: Dynamic repository inventory; no snapshot count recorded here.
sources.notes: Public Python-package advisory inventory. Use IDs, affected ranges, and references to select candidates, then independently locate an authorized upstream revision and reproduce a differential oracle.

sources.name: GitHub Advisory Database / Global Security Advisories
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 for github/advisory-database repository; API advisory metadata should be used subject to GitHub terms.
sources.available_cases: Dynamic API inventory; no snapshot count recorded here.
sources.notes: The documented API exposes GHSA and optional CVE IDs, package ecosystem/name, affected ranges, first patched version, references, and CWEs. It is an authoritative selection feed, not an execution oracle or a guarantee that an upstream fixing commit is available.

sources.name: OSV.dev
sources.license: Aggregated entries retain source-specific provenance and licensing; consult each entry/source.
frameworks: PyPI plus other OpenSSF Vulnerability Format adopters
sources.available_cases: Dynamic aggregated inventory; no snapshot count recorded here.
sources.notes: OSV aggregates databases adopting the OpenSSF Vulnerability format and supports version- or commit-hash queries. Use it to cross-reference IDs and affected versions, not as proof that a benchmark case executes locally.

sources.name: OWASP Benchmark for Python v0.1
frameworks: Runnable Python web application for SAST, DAST, and IAST
sources.available_cases: No stable published count in the preliminary v0.1 README.
sources.notes: Intentionally vulnerable test suite, useful for scanner and harness integration. It is explicitly not a source of real historical CVE/GHSA candidate cases in this catalog.
